subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What are the main kinds of issues these support tickets are about?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/taxonomy of support ticket issues -- classifying what each ticket is about across its lifecycle (type of issue, where it occurs, why, and how it is resolved)

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query -- the kind of issue (bug, feature_request, outage, etc.). This is the core focus facet.

per_column.name: primary_product_area
per_column.rationale: Locates the issue within the product surface, a coherent facet characterising WHERE an issue arises, differentiating issue kinds by domain.

per_column.name: root_cause_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Characterises WHY the issue occurred; a coherent explanatory facet of an issue, adding analytical depth beyond bare category.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: Characterises HOW the issue was addressed; a coherent facet of the issue lifecycle that further distinguishes issue kinds.

judge.rationale: All four columns centre on a single coherent, data-inferable focus: the taxonomy/characterisation of support ticket issues. They form a well-structured multi-facet decomposition (what the issue is, where it lives, why it happened, how it was resolved) at a useful, differentiated granularity -- not a single restatement nor generic noise. issue_category directly serves the query, and the other three enrich it with orthogonal but tightly related facets. The implied focus is highly actionable: an analyst can prioritise categories, spot root-cause clusters, and align resolution strategies. Minor deduction on structure because root_cause and resolution overlap somewhat in signal (e.g., 'code_hotfix_or_rollback' mirrors 'recent_deployment'), and 'not_present' dominating root_cause_mechanism suggests sparse inference for that facet, but the set remains coherent and analytically sound.
